Reproducing Yu et al. (2016) from dandiset 000005¶

Paper: Yu J, Gutnisky DA, Hires SA, Svoboda K (2016). Layer 4 fast-spiking interneurons filter thalamocortical signals during active somatosensation. Nature Neuroscience 19:1647-1657, doi:10.1038/nn.4412.

Dandiset: DANDI:000005, version 0.220126.1853. The paper cites no dandiset version (it predates the archive). 0.220126.1853 is the only published version, so it is pinned; the draft (last modified 2026-02-12) lists the same 148 asset paths and sizes (printed below). The version is the same as that of the earlier attempt, 000005-yu-2016-01.

Claims: claims/000005/10.1038-nn.4412.yaml, written by a reader from the version of record with its Online Methods and the supplement (Supplementary Figures 1 to 14, Supplementary Tables 1 and 2), and checked by a second reader on 2026-10-20. It replaces the claims file of the earlier attempt, which was written from the abstract. The ids of eight earlier claims are kept; their criteria are new. The paper's data statement points to CRCNS ssc-7; no analysis code was found.

This is a repeat attempt. The earlier attempt's findings are checked again in the data check.

Outside input: Supplementary Table 1 of the paper (the mouse line of each mouse), read at run time from the supplement PDF on the publisher's site. It is used to name the mouse lines that the files leave blank and to compare the cells per line with Supplementary Table 2.

Readings. The claims file names readings for details the paper leaves open (O1 filter direction, O2 samples of the rank-sum test, O3 threshold rule, O4 resting Vm, O5 light windows, O6 fraction of control, O7 laser powers, O8 derivative, O9 time of a crossing bin, O10 whisking-onset windows, O11 touches bounding whisking epochs). Each is run where it applies.

Answers. A reader answered this attempt's seven questions on 2026-10-20 (questions/000005.yaml), and the claims file was updated: dVm/dt is taken at the recording's sampling rate, not in 1 ms bins (O8); the PSTH latency is run with the bin's left edge and its centre (O9); fs-touch-response runs four FS readings (driven at p < 0.001 or p < 0.01, each with and without the waveform boundary); behavior-false-alarms runs the chi-squared test with and without Yates's correction; the paired tests of thalamus-drives-fs are two-sided; behavior-touches runs every trial and trials without light; exc-vm-touch-whisking runs the whisking-onset and touch readings O10 and O11. The sections of the claims these bear on say what each answer changed. Cell groups hold the cells of every mouse ("all"), since the files do not mark the ION-cut mice; a variant without the mice flagged as lacking touch input ("no_flagged") is shown and does not decide an outcome.

Revision after the first verification round. The tag test now counts every 5 ms pulse of the 5 and 10 Hz trains (the earlier rule kept only pulses with no other pulse within 100 ms); the touch readings O11 are run for every claim on whisking epochs, and O10 and O11 for every claim on whisking onsets; trials of a whole-cell cell held near 0 mV are left out at rest; and the data check adds spike detection quality, the tagging coverage of every VGAT-ChR2 cell, the injected current of every file, the pole times and the ION-cut candidates. New outputs show the cause of the near-zero Vm latencies and the stability of the AUC claims over 20 seeds.

import re
import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import yu2016

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 300)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
recs = yu2016.load_all()
vpm = [r for r in recs if r["kind"] == "VPM"]
l4 = [r for r in recs if r["kind"] == "L4"]
by_path = {r["path"]: r for r in l4}
print(f"loaded {len(recs)} files from dandiset {yu2016.DANDISET_ID} version {yu2016.DANDISET_VERSION} "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

loaded 148 files from dandiset 000005 version 0.220126.1853 in 355 s

Data check¶

No random numbers are drawn in the data check. Each check of the metadata against the values is stated under its output.

0.220126.1853 is the only published version, and the draft holds the same asset paths and sizes. The 18 VPM files come from 6 mice and the 130 L4 files from 49 others; all 55 mice are in Supplementary Table 1. Where a file gives a genotype it agrees with the table's mouse line, but 9 mice have none (the 6 VPM mice and 3 L4 mice) and the 5 SOM-IRES-Cre x Ai32 mice are given as Ai32 (earlier finding 3, still present). The files hold no surgery, lesion, opsin or notes field, and no text names ION, infraorbital, nerve, transection, cut, sham or eNpHR (earlier findings 2 and 5, still present). Every L4 file gives barrel cortex, layer 4, at 0.42 to 0.62 mm (earlier finding 4, still present). The VPM files hold no photostimulation series, and no L4 file is outside barrel cortex, so the thalamic multiunit recordings of Fig. 6b,c are not in the dandiset.

The recording mode in the session description disagrees with the trace for 24 files, all from PV-IRES-Cre mice: 23 described as whole-cell sit near 0 mV with a 1 to 100 Hz s.d. of 0.08 to 0.3 mV and small extracellular spikes, as cell-attached recordings do, and one described as juxtacellular sits near -65 mV (earlier finding 6, still present). The mode read from the trace is used below; the stored trace is in mV (conversion 0.001 to volts), which the whole-cell resting potentials confirm. The trace is sampled at 10 kHz up to March 2015 and at 20 kHz from late August 2015, which only the timestamps state (earlier finding 8, still present); timestamps start at the trial start and no sample lies outside a trial.

New: the injected current (CurrentClampStimulus) is stored with unit amperes and conversion 1e-6, so a stored -0.1 would be -0.1 uA. The end-of-trial test pulse, which the Methods give as -0.1 nA, is stored as about -0.1 in 14 of the 57 whole-cell files, so the stored values are in nA and the conversion is wrong by a factor of 1,000. Only one whole-cell file has trials held near 0 mV (13 trials of the PV-ChR2 cell); these trials are now left out of every measure at rest. 17 cell-attached files of VGAT-ChR2 mice carry a stored current of about 1.9 in every trial, but their traces sit near 0 mV with a 1 to 100 Hz s.d. of at most 0.33 mV (whole-cell files: median 1.95 mV), so they are not whole-cell cells held near 0 mV; no trial of any other file has a median current above 0.5. The trial-median trace of the cell-attached files spans -21.85 to 20.72 mV, and only one file has a trial below -20 mV. So the recordings of L4 excitatory neurons depolarized to reveal inhibition (Fig. 3, 6 neurons) are not in the dandiset. Two cell-attached files have a larger slow component (1.1 and 1.3 mV), still far below the whole-cell values; both are from PV-IRES-Cre mice.

The whisker variables are at 1 kHz, 5,000 samples (5 s) per trial, in degrees with a plausible range. 8 files name no principal whisker (earlier finding 9, still present); they are left out of every measure that needs touch or whisking. In the L4 files first_touch_time matches the touch series only when multiplied by 1000 (0.956 of trials), so the latency was divided by 1000 once too often; in the VPM files it is correct (earlier finding 7, still present). The analysis uses the touch series. The pole times are not scaled like first_touch_time: in the L4 files pole_in_time lies 0.832 s after the trial start in the median trial (0.832 to 1.084 s), pole_out_time 2.835 s in the median, and the first touch follows pole in by 0.528 s in the median and never precedes it, so the no-touch windows of AUC reading (a), drawn between them, lie where the pole is present (0.899 of L4 trials have pole in and out 0.5 s or more apart within the 5 s video). In the VPM files each file names one principal whisker, though the session description says each unit has its own: 11 of the 20 units in files with more than one tracked whisker respond most to another whisker, some strongly (earlier finding 9, now shown per unit).

# Alignment of spikes and behaviour: each cell's touch response (spikes per touch, VPM or Fig. 5 definition) and
# phase-coupling r2 with its spikes in their own trial, and moved to the next trial at the same time after its start.
rows = []
for r in recs:
    b = r["beh"]
    if b["principal"] is None:
        continue
    allm = np.ones(len(r["trials"]), bool) if r["kind"] == "VPM" else ~yu2016.lit_trials(r["light"], r["trials"])
    cells = [(u["unit"], u["spikes"]) for u in r["units"]] if r["kind"] == "VPM" else [(0, r["spikes"])]
    for unit, sp in cells:
        if len(sp) < 50:
            continue
        out = {"kind": r["kind"], "path": r["path"], "unit": unit}
        for tag, s in (("true", sp), ("shift", yu2016.shift_spikes(sp, r["trials"]))):
            c = yu2016.counts_1k(s, b)
            c = np.where(allm[np.clip(b["trial"], 0, None)], c, 0)
            out[f"spt_{tag}"] = yu2016.spikes_per_touch(c, b["trial"], yu2016.touches(b, allm), "vpm" if r["kind"] == "VPM" else "cortex5")["spt"]
            vals, _ = yu2016.phase_binned(b, "filtfilt", count=c)
            out[f"r2_{tag}"] = yu2016.phase_fit(vals)["r2"]
        rows.append(out)
align = pd.DataFrame(rows)
for kind, g in align.groupby("kind"):
    g = g.dropna()
    print(f"{kind}: {len(g)} units or cells with at least 50 spikes. Spikes per touch, median own trial {g.spt_true.median():.3f}, "
          f"next trial {g.spt_shift.median():.3f}, larger in own trial for {(g.spt_true > g.spt_shift).sum()} "
          f"(signed-rank p = {stats.wilcoxon(g.spt_true, g.spt_shift).pvalue:.2g}); phase r2, median own {g.r2_true.median():.2f}, "
          f"next {g.r2_shift.median():.2f} (p = {stats.wilcoxon(g.r2_true, g.r2_shift).pvalue:.2g}); r2 > 0.25 own "
          f"{(g.r2_true > 0.25).mean():.2f}, next {(g.r2_shift > 0.25).mean():.2f}")
bad = align[(align.spt_true <= align.spt_shift) & (align.r2_true <= align.r2_shift)]
print("Units or cells where neither measure is larger in their own trial:", len(bad), "of", len(align))

Spikes and behaviour share a clock in the data as a whole: for VPM units and L4 cells, the touch response and the phase coupling are larger with spikes in their own trial than moved to the next trial (signed-rank p printed above). This cannot be shown for a cell that responds to neither; 9 of 121 such cells are consistent with the clock, not shown to share it. No two files share a trace, a VPM spike train or a trial table, so no recording is deposited twice. Chronic VPM units recorded on several days may be the same neurons; the files give no identifiers that link them, and each unit is counted once, as in the paper's 29.

# Cell classes, by the rules of the claims file's header (see the helper's docstring for the tests):
# FS: in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, driven by 5 ms light pulses at the cortical site within 5 ms of onset (isolated pulses,
#     the pulses of 5 and 10 Hz trains, one-sided binomial test against the same 5 ms 50 ms earlier; the paper gives no test, so the claims file names
#     p < 0.001 and p < 0.01 as readings) and inside the Supp. Fig. 6 waveform boundary (cell-attached cells only;
#     with and without the boundary are readings of fs-touch-response); in PV-IRES-Cre mice, PV cells inactivated by the eNpHR light (rate inside
#     the light lower than in the same span of trials without light, Mann-Whitney over trials, p < 0.05); in lines
#     without a tag, whole-cell cells with spikes no wider than 0.35 ms at half height (the largest FS width the Methods
#     give). Every other L4 cell is excitatory (E).
def light_effect(r):
    """Spike rate inside the light (median span of the lit trials) against the same span of trials without light."""
    out = None
    ctl = ~yu2016.lit_trials(r["light"], r["trials"])
    for site, L in r["light"].items():
        w = yu2016.light_windows(r["light"], site, r["trials"])
        if len(w) == 0 or not (np.diff(L["pulses"], axis=1) > 0.1).any():
            continue
        lit = np.zeros(len(r["trials"]), bool)
        lit[w.trial.to_numpy(int)] = True
        win = (float(np.median(w.rel_start)), float(np.median(w.rel_stop)))
        sp, st = np.sort(r["spikes"]), r["trials"].start.to_numpy()
        per = lambda m: (np.searchsorted(sp, st[m] + win[1]) - np.searchsorted(sp, st[m] + win[0])) / (win[1] - win[0])
        a, b = per(lit), per(ctl)
        p = stats.mannwhitneyu(a, b, alternative="less").pvalue if len(a) and len(b) and (a.sum() + b.sum()) > 0 else np.nan
        out = {"light_site": L["region"], "light_win": win, "lit_trials": int(lit.sum()), "ctl_trials": int(ctl.sum()),
               "rate_ctl": b.mean(), "rate_light": a.mean(), "light_p_lower": p}
    return out

rows = []
for r in l4:
    row = {"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "line": line_of[r["subject"]], "mode": r["mode"], "spikes": len(r["spikes"]),
           "fwhm_ms": r["fwhm_ms"], "ca_duration_ms": r["ca_duration_ms"], "ca_ratio": r["ca_ratio"], "pw": r["beh"]["principal"] is not None}
    best = None
    for site, L in r["light"].items():
        if "vS1" not in L["region"]:
            continue
        lr = yu2016.light_pulse_response(r["light"], r["spikes"], site)
        if lr["n_pulses"] >= yu2016.TAG_MIN_PULSES and (best is None or lr["p_evoked"] - lr["p_base"] > best["p_evoked"] - best["p_base"]):
            on_ = yu2016.tag_pulses(r["light"], site)
            ipi = np.diff(L["pulses"][:, 0])
            best = {**lr, "tag_site": L["region"], "ipi_ms": float(np.median(ipi[ipi < 1]) * 1000) if np.any(ipi < 1) else np.nan,
                    **{f"{k}_{rule}": yu2016.light_pulse_response(r["light"], r["spikes"], site, rule).get(k, np.nan)
                       for rule in ("first", "isolated") for k in ("n_pulses", "p_value")}}
    if best:
        row.update(tag_site=best["tag_site"], pulses=best["n_pulses"], p_evoked=best["p_evoked"], p_base=best["p_base"],
                   tag_p=best["p_value"], tag_latency_ms=best["median_latency_ms"], ipi_ms=best["ipi_ms"],
                   pulses_first=best["n_pulses_first"], tag_p_first=best["p_value_first"],
                   pulses_isolated=best["n_pulses_isolated"], tag_p_isolated=best["p_value_isolated"])
    le = light_effect(r) if row["line"] == "PV-IRES-Cre" else None
    if le:
        row.update(le)
    rows.append(row)
cells = pd.DataFrame(rows)
cells["tag_tested"] = cells.get("pulses", pd.Series(np.nan, index=cells.index)).notna()
cells["driven"] = cells.tag_p < yu2016.TAG_MAX_P
cells["driven_01"] = cells.tag_p < 0.01
cells["in_boundary"] = (cells.ca_duration_ms < yu2016.FS_MAX_DURATION_MS) & (cells.ca_ratio < yu2016.FS_MAX_RATIO)
cells["pv_inactivated"] = (cells.line == "PV-IRES-Cre") & (cells.light_p_lower < 0.05) & (cells.rate_light < cells.rate_ctl)
untagged_lines = ~cells.line.isin(["VGAT-ChR2-EYFP", "PV-IRES-Cre"])
cells["thin_wc"] = untagged_lines & (cells["mode"] == "whole-cell") & (cells.fwhm_ms <= 0.35)

def classify(driven_col="driven", boundary=True):
    driven = (cells.line == "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP") & cells[driven_col]
    fs = driven & ((cells["mode"] == "whole-cell") | cells.in_boundary) if boundary else driven
    cls = np.where(fs | cells.pv_inactivated | cells.thin_wc, "FS", "E")
    # driven (GABAergic) cells outside the boundary are neither FS nor excitatory (Supp. Fig. 6)
    return np.where(driven & ~fs, "other GABAergic", cls)

cells["cls"] = classify()                        # the claims file's rule: driven (p < 0.001) and inside the boundary
cells["cls_01"] = classify("driven_01")          # reading: driven at p < 0.01
cells["cls_tag"] = classify(boundary=False)      # driven at p < 0.001, any waveform (reading of fs-touch-response only)
cells["cls_01_tag"] = classify("driven_01", boundary=False)   # driven at p < 0.01, any waveform (same)
print("L4 cells by mouse line, mode and class (driven at p < 0.001 and, cell-attached, inside the waveform boundary):")
print(pd.crosstab([cells.line, cells["mode"]], cells.cls).to_string())
print("Cells whose class changes with the tag at p < 0.01:", cells[cells.cls != cells.cls_01].path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:40].tolist())
print("Cells that are FS without the waveform boundary (driven, outside it):",
      cells[cells.cls != cells.cls_tag][["path", "ca_duration_ms", "ca_ratio"]].assign(path=lambda x: x.path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:36]).round(2).values.tolist())
vg = cells[(cells.line == "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP")]
print(f"\nVGAT-ChR2 cells: {len(vg)}; tested with at least 10 tag pulses at a cortical site {int(vg.tag_tested.sum())}; driven (p < 0.001) "
      f"{int(vg.driven.sum())}, (p < 0.01) {int(vg.driven_01.sum())}")
d = vg[vg.driven]
print("Driven cells: evoked spike probability median", round(d.p_evoked.median(), 2), "(baseline", round(d.p_base.median(), 2),
      "); first-spike latency median", round(d.tag_latency_ms.median(), 2), "ms, range", round(d.tag_latency_ms.min(), 2), "to",
      round(d.tag_latency_ms.max(), 2))
print("VGAT-ChR2 cells without at least 10 tag pulses at a cortical site:", vg[~vg.tag_tested][["path", "mode", "spikes", "fwhm_ms"]]
      .assign(path=lambda x: x.path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:40]).round(2).to_dict("records"))
print("\nTagging coverage, every VGAT-ChR2 cell with a cortical site: tag pulses (5 and 10 Hz trains, the rule used), median interval "
      "between pulses (ms), and the tag p under the rule used, the first pulse of each train, and isolated pulses (the earlier rule):")
print(vg[vg.tag_tested][["path", "mode", "spikes", "pulses", "ipi_ms", "tag_p", "pulses_first", "tag_p_first", "pulses_isolated", "tag_p_isolated",
                         "tag_latency_ms"]].assign(path=lambda x: x.path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:34]).round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("Driven at p < 0.001 under each pulse rule: trains (used)", int((vg.tag_p < 0.001).sum()), "; first pulse of each train",
      int((vg.tag_p_first < 0.001).sum()), "; isolated pulses", int((vg.tag_p_isolated < 0.001).sum()))
print("Cells driven under the rule used and not under the first-pulse rule:",
      vg[(vg.tag_p < 0.001) & ~(vg.tag_p_first < 0.001)].path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:34].tolist())
ca = vg[vg["mode"] == "cell-attached"]
print("\nCell-attached VGAT-ChR2 cells, Supp. Fig. 6 measures (peak-to-trough duration ms, peak/trough ratio), by tag:")
print(ca.groupby("driven")[["ca_duration_ms", "ca_ratio"]].describe().round(2).T.to_string())
print("Driven cell-attached cells inside the boundary (duration < 0.27 ms and ratio < 2.8):", int((ca.driven & ca.in_boundary).sum()),
      "of", int(ca.driven.sum()), "; undriven inside it:", int((~ca.driven & ca.in_boundary).sum()), "of", int((~ca.driven).sum()))
pv = cells[cells.line == "PV-IRES-Cre"].dropna(subset=["rate_ctl"])
print(f"\nPV-IRES-Cre cells with the eNpHR light: {len(pv)} (light span {sorted(set(tuple(np.round(w, 2)) for w in pv.light_win))[:3]} ...); "
      f"rate lower with light (p < 0.05): {int(pv.pv_inactivated.sum())}; ratio light/control below 0.5 among them: "
      f"{int((pv.pv_inactivated & (pv.rate_light < 0.5 * pv.rate_ctl)).sum())}")
print(pv[pv.pv_inactivated | (pv.rate_light < 0.8 * pv.rate_ctl)][["path", "mode", "spikes", "rate_ctl", "rate_light", "light_p_lower", "ca_duration_ms", "ca_ratio"]]
      .assign(path=lambda x: x.path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:40]).round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nThin-spiking whole-cell cells of lines without a tag:", cells[cells.thin_wc][["path", "line", "fwhm_ms", "spikes"]]
      .assign(path=lambda x: x.path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:40]).round(2).to_dict("records"))
print("Whole-cell spike width at half height (ms) of the lines without a tag:",
      cells[untagged_lines & (cells["mode"] == "whole-cell")][["line", "fwhm_ms"]].round(2).values.tolist())
# Against Supplementary Table 2 (cells per line, mode and type; control and ION-cut cells together)
paper = pd.DataFrame([("VGAT-ChR2-EYFP", "whole-cell", 32, 5), ("VGAT-ChR2-EYFP", "cell-attached", 6, 24),
                      ("PV-IRES-Cre", "whole-cell", 5, 0), ("PV-IRES-Cre", "cell-attached", 38, 4),
                      ("PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32", "whole-cell", 1, 0), ("C57BL/6", "whole-cell", 7, 1), ("PV-ChR2", "whole-cell", 0, 1),
                      ("SOM-IRES-Cre x Ai32", "whole-cell", 1, 0), ("SOM-IRES-Cre x Ai32", "cell-attached", 4, 0)],
                     columns=["line", "mode", "paper_E", "paper_FS"])
ours = cells.groupby(["line", "mode"]).cls.value_counts().unstack(fill_value=0).reindex(columns=["E", "FS", "other GABAergic"], fill_value=0)
cmp_ = paper.merge(ours.reset_index().rename(columns={"E": "files_E", "FS": "files_FS", "other GABAergic": "files_other"}),
                   on=["line", "mode"], how="outer").fillna(0)
print("\nCells per line, mode and type: Supplementary Table 2 (E includes 9 whole-cell ION-cut cells, FS 10 cell-attached ION-cut cells) "
      "against the files:")
print(cmp_.to_string(index=False))
print("Totals: paper E", int(cmp_.paper_E.sum()), "FS", int(cmp_.paper_FS.sum()), "; files E", int(cmp_.files_E.sum()), "FS",
      int(cmp_.files_FS.sum()), "other GABAergic", int(cmp_.files_other.sum()))

No file names the cell type of its L4 neuron (earlier finding 1, still present), so the classes are built from the data by the claims file's rules. The tag test now counts every pulse of the 5 and 10 Hz trains. In VGAT-ChR2 mice, 41 cells have at least 10 tag pulses at a cortical site and 24 of them are driven within 5 ms (latency 1.6 to 4.6 ms), the same 24 as under the earlier rule of isolated pulses; the first pulse of each train alone drives 8, since many cells had few trains. Supplementary Table 2 counts 29 FS cells there (19 control and 10 ION-cut). The other 26 VGAT-ChR2 cells have fewer than 10 short pulses at any cortical site (the tagging table lists every cell tested; the list above names the others, among them the cells with 16,350 and 11,087 spikes), so no pulse rule can test them and they count as excitatory. The waveform boundary of Supplementary Fig. 6, as read in the claims file, keeps 12 of the 20 driven cell-attached cells; the other 8 are GABAergic but outside it and are left out of both classes. Their measures (duration 0.3 to 0.9 ms, ratio 2.26 to 19.23) follow the figure's inset (peak, the trough after it and the time between them), but 4 of these driven cells have ratios of 12.2 to 19.2, beyond the figure's axis (8), where the figure has no cell, so the measure here does not place every cell as the figure does. The tag at p < 0.01 adds 3 cells, all outside the boundary, so it changes no FS group. In PV-IRES-Cre mice 3 cells are inhibited by the light (the paper has 4 PV cells); in the lines without a tag one whole-cell cell has spikes 0.25 ms wide. The PV-ChR2 cell, FS in Supplementary Table 2, has spikes 0.44 ms wide here and counts as excitatory. The result: 20 FS cells against the table's 35 (25 control and 10 ION-cut), and 102 excitatory cells against 94.

# Spike detection (standard choices, helper docstring) checked against what a spike train allows: the fraction of interspike
# intervals under 1.5 ms (refractory violations), and the size of the detected spikes (whole-cell, median prominence in mV,
# detection needs 20; cell-attached, median peak in robust s.d. of the high-passed trace, detection needs 6). Rates by mode and
# class are set against the paper's.
sq = []
for r in l4:
    sp = np.sort(r["spikes"])
    isi = np.diff(sp)
    c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
    sq.append({"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "line": c.line, "mode": r["mode"], "cls": c.cls, "spikes": len(sp),
               "isi_viol": float(np.mean(isi < 0.0015)) if len(isi) else np.nan, "spike_size": r["spike_size"],
               "rate_all": len(sp) / (len(r["trials"]) * yu2016.ANALYSIS_END_S)})
spikeq = pd.DataFrame(sq)
print("L4 cells, by mode and class: fraction of interspike intervals under 1.5 ms, spike size, and spikes/s over the first 5 s of every trial")
print(spikeq.groupby(["mode", "cls"]).agg(cells=("path", "size"), isi_viol_median=("isi_viol", "median"), isi_viol_max=("isi_viol", "max"),
                                          above_1pct=("isi_viol", lambda x: int((x > 0.01).sum())), size_median=("spike_size", "median"),
                                          size_min=("spike_size", "min"), rate_median=("rate_all", "median"), rate_mean=("rate_all", "mean")).round(4).to_string())
print("Cells with more than 1% of intervals under 1.5 ms:", spikeq[spikeq.isi_viol > 0.01][["path", "mode", "cls", "spikes", "isi_viol", "spike_size", "rate_all"]]
      .assign(path=lambda d: d.path.str.split("/").str[1].str[:34]).round(3).to_dict("records"))
vq = [float(np.mean(np.diff(np.sort(u["spikes"])) < 0.0015)) for r in vpm for u in r["units"] if len(u["spikes"]) > 1]
print("VPM units (sorted in the files): fraction under 1.5 ms, median", round(float(np.median(vq)), 4), ", max", round(float(np.max(vq)), 4))
e_ = spikeq[spikeq.cls == "E"]
print("E cells, spikes/s over all time, by mode: whole-cell mean", round(e_[e_["mode"] == "whole-cell"].rate_all.mean(), 3), ", cell-attached mean",
      round(e_[e_["mode"] == "cell-attached"].rate_all.mean(), 3), "; the paper's E rates are 0.4 (nonwhisking) and 0.6 (whisking) spikes/s over 85 cells")
def dead_time(sp, dead=0.002):
    """Spike times with every spike less than `dead` s after the last kept spike removed."""
    keep, last = [], -np.inf
    for t in np.sort(sp):
        if t - last >= dead:
            keep.append(t)
            last = t
    return np.array(keep)
ca_e = [r for r in l4 if r["mode"] == "cell-attached" and cells.set_index("path").cls[r["path"]] == "E"]
r0 = np.array([len(r["spikes"]) / (len(r["trials"]) * yu2016.ANALYSIS_END_S) for r in ca_e])
r1 = np.array([len(dead_time(r["spikes"])) / (len(r["trials"]) * yu2016.ANALYSIS_END_S) for r in ca_e])
print(f"Cell-attached E cells: with a 2 ms dead time imposed on the detected spikes the mean rate goes from {r0.mean():.2f} to {r1.mean():.2f} "
      f"spikes/s (median {np.median(r0):.2f} to {np.median(r1):.2f}), so double detection removes {1 - r1.sum() / r0.sum():.3f} of the spikes")
for thr in (6, 8, 10):
    big = e_[(e_["mode"] == "cell-attached")]
    print(f"Cell-attached E cells whose median spike is at least {thr} robust s.d.: {int((big.spike_size >= thr).sum())} of {len(big)}")

Spike detection. Whole-cell spikes are clean: no whole-cell E cell has more than 0.01% of its interspike intervals under 1.5 ms, and the median spike is 42.8 mV high. In cell-attached cells the median spike is 20.9 robust s.d. (E) and 46.4 (FS) above the noise, far above the 6 s.d. threshold (45 of 50 cell-attached E cells at 10 s.d. or more), but the median E cell has 5.2% of its intervals under 1.5 ms (40 of 50 above 1%), so some spikes are detected twice or a neighbouring unit is picked up. Imposing a 2 ms dead time removes 8.1% of the cell-attached E spikes and lowers their mean rate only from 6.20 to 5.70 spikes/s. Over all time, cell-attached E cells fire 6.20 spikes/s on average and whole-cell E cells 0.88, against the paper's 0.4 and 0.6 spikes/s for its 85 E cells. Double detection does not explain the high cell-attached rates, which drive the rate values of exc-mainly-touch, fs-suppress-movement-spiking and auc-groups. Whether these cells fire this fast or the recordings hold more than one unit cannot be told from the files. The sorted VPM units have a median of 0.97% of intervals under 1.5 ms.

Measures for every unit and cell¶

Each VPM unit and L4 cell with a named principal whisker, over its trials without light, by the definitions of the helper module.

# Every measure of every VPM unit and L4 cell over its trials without light (claims, Measures; helper docstring).
def ctl_mask(r):
    """Trials without light, and (whole-cell) not held near 0 mV by current."""
    if r["kind"] == "VPM":
        return np.ones(len(r["trials"]), bool)
    return ~yu2016.lit_trials(r["light"], r["trials"]) & ~r["held_trials"]

rows, vrows = [], []
for r in recs:
    b = r["beh"]
    if b["principal"] is None:
        continue
    m = ctl_mask(r)
    if r["kind"] == "VPM":
        for u in r["units"]:
            rows.append({"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "unit": u["unit"], "cls": "VPM", "mode": "probe",
                         **yu2016.spike_measures(u["spikes"], b, m, "vpm", np.random.default_rng(u["unit"]))})
        continue
    c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
    rows.append({"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "unit": 0, "cls": c.cls, "mode": r["mode"],
                 **yu2016.spike_measures(r["spikes"], b, m, "cortex5", np.random.default_rng(0), fs_fit=True)})
    if r["mode"] == "whole-cell":
        for filt in yu2016.FILTERS:
            for reading in ("a", "b"):
                v = yu2016.vm_measures(r, m, filt, reading)
                vrows.append({"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "filt": filt, "O3": reading, "touch_avg_n": r["touch_avg_n"],
                              **{k: x for k, x in v.items() if np.ndim(x) == 0}, "touch_pre": v["touch_pre"], "touch_dvm": v["touch_dvm"],
                              "whisk_pre": v["whisk_pre"], "whisk_dvm": v["whisk_dvm"]})
meas = pd.DataFrame(rows)
vmm = pd.DataFrame(vrows)
for col in ["cls_01", "cls_tag", "cls_01_tag"]:

      vmm.path.nunique())

The files do not mark the 9 ION-cut mice. In 3 VGAT-ChR2 mice no cell has a touch input (the 8 whole-cell excitatory cells of anm318530 and anm318532 have average touch PSPs of 0.75 mV or less), and in anm275231 and anm273341 the mice performed below 0.5 correct. These 4 mice are consistent with the ION-cut mice of Fig. 7 and are left out in the variant "no_flagged". The rule was chosen after seeing the values, and it selects by touch responses, so it favours claims about touch; it never decides an outcome. It finds 8 of the table's 9 whole-cell ION-cut cells and 7 of its 10 cell-attached ones (3 of which are outside the waveform boundary here). Supplementary Table 2 suggests the ION-cut mice had no fibre in VPM: of the 27 VGAT-ChR2 mice with L4 cells, 12 have a light site labelled VPM and none of them is flagged, and the 4 flagged mice are among the 15 without one. The other 11 mice without a VPM site include 8 whose cells have touch PSPs of 3.85 to 10.84 mV, so they are not ION-cut. The remaining 3 (anm281589, anm281592 and anm318531) have no cell with a touch PSP of 1 mV or more (anm281589 has no whole-cell cell), but each has a cell whose spikes per touch has a 95% interval above zero, so by this attempt's rule they have touch input and are weak candidates at most. That makes at most 7 candidates for the paper's 9 ION-cut mice, so either some ION-cut mice had a VPM fibre or the hint does not hold, and the files cannot confirm which mice were cut.

The new findings of this attempt are the current conversion, the missing recordings (Fig. 3 depolarized cells, Fig. 6b,c thalamic multiunits, Supplementary Fig. 10 histology), the 50 Hz trains, and the two spellings of the no-lick trial type.

# Groups used below. The files do not mark ION-cut mice, so every group holds the cells of all mice ("all"); the
# variant leaves out the VGAT-ChR2 mice flagged as lacking touch input or performing below 0.5 ("no_flagged").
FS_READINGS = {"tag p<0.001, boundary": "cls", "tag p<0.01, boundary": "cls_01"}
FS_VARIANT = {"tag p<0.001, any waveform (variant)": "cls_tag"}
# fs-touch-response names four readings of the FS group (answer of 2026-10-20)
FS_READINGS_TOUCH = {"(a)(i) p<0.001, boundary": "cls", "(a)(ii) p<0.001, no boundary": "cls_tag",
                     "(b)(i) p<0.01, boundary": "cls_01", "(b)(ii) p<0.01, no boundary": "cls_01_tag"}

def group(cls, mode=None, sel="all", col="cls"):
    g = meas[meas[col] == cls] if cls != "VPM" else meas[meas.cls == "VPM"]
    if mode:
        g = g[g["mode"] == mode]
    if sel == "no_flagged":
        g = g[~g.subject.isin(flagged)]
    return g

def o11_group(g, o11):
    """`g` with its whisking-epoch columns taken under touch reading O11 `o11`."""
    x = meas_o11[meas_o11.O11 == o11].set_index(["path", "unit"])[RATE_COLS]
    return g.drop(columns=RATE_COLS).join(x, on=["path", "unit"])

def rate_summary(g):
    """Per O11 reading, filter (O1) and rank-sum samples (O2): increases, decreases, rates, the signed-rank test of whisking
    against nonwhisking rate, the cells with r2 > 0.25, and the cells that multiplex (spikes per touch above zero and a
    significant whisking change)."""
    rows = []
    for o11 in yu2016.O11:
        go = o11_group(g, o11)
        for f in yu2016.FILTERS:
            for o2 in ("O2a", "O2b"):
                rows.append({"O11": o11, "filter": f, "samples": o2, "n": len(go), "increase": int((go[f"{f}:{o2}"] == 1).sum()),
                             "decrease": int((go[f"{f}:{o2}"] == -1).sum()), "nonwhisk_mean": go[f"{f}:rate_nonwhisk"].mean(),
                             "nonwhisk_median": go[f"{f}:rate_nonwhisk"].median(), "whisk_mean": go[f"{f}:rate_whisk"].mean(),
                             "signed_rank_p": wilcox(go[f"{f}:rate_nonwhisk"], go[f"{f}:rate_whisk"]),
                             "whisk_higher": int((go[f"{f}:rate_whisk"] > go[f"{f}:rate_nonwhisk"]).sum()),
                             "r2_above_0.25": int((go[f"{f}:r2"] > 0.25).sum()), "multiplex": int(((go.spt_lo > 0) & (go[f"{f}:{o2}"] != 0)).sum())})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def ranges(t, cols):
    """Range of each column over the rows of a reading table."""
    return {c: (float(f"{t[c].min():.3g}"), float(f"{t[c].max():.3g}")) for c in cols}

def fmt_p(t):
    """The p-value columns of a table as text with two significant digits."""
    return t.assign(**{c: t[c].map(lambda x: "%.2g" % x) for c in t.columns if c.startswith("p_") or c.endswith("_p")})

def wilcox(x, y, alternative="two-sided"):
    x, y = np.asarray(x, float), np.asarray(y, float)
    ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    if ok.sum() < 2 or np.all(x[ok] == y[ok]):
        return np.nan
    return float(stats.wilcoxon(x[ok], y[ok], alternative=alternative).pvalue)

def within(value, expected, tol):
    return bool(np.isfinite(value) and abs(value - expected) <= tol)

behavior-touches¶

Mice touched the pole often when it was within reach (lick trials, 5.7 +- 5.3 touches per trial over 4,147 trials) and rarely when it was distal (0.9 +- 3.4 over 4,173 trials); performance was 0.72 +- 0.11 in cortical and 0.71 +- 0.07 in VPM recordings.

In [13]:
def touch_counts(r, whiskers="pw", ctl_only=True):
    b, tr = r["beh"], r["trials"]
    if b["principal"] is None:
        return None
    m = ctl_mask(r) if ctl_only else np.ones(len(tr), bool)
    if whiskers == "pw":
        on_t = b["t"][b["touch_on"]]
    else:
        on_t = np.sort(np.concatenate([b["t"][w["on"]] for w in b["whisker_touches"].values()]))
    k = yu2016.per_trial_index(on_t, tr)
    n = np.bincount(k[k >= 0], minlength=len(tr))
    return pd.DataFrame({"type": tr.type.str.capitalize().to_numpy()[m], "touches": n[m], "correct": tr.response.isin(["Hit", "CR"]).to_numpy()[m]})

# reading (a): the 111 control cortical cells cannot be identified (no ION-cut marks), so every cortical cell counts, as in every
# other group; the cells of the flagged mice left out are a variant that does not decide
ctl_cortex = meas[meas.cls != "VPM"].path.unique()
nf_cortex = meas[(meas.cls != "VPM") & ~meas.subject.isin(flagged)].path.unique()
res = []
for rec_set, paths in (("a: control cortical recordings", set(ctl_cortex)), ("b: all sessions", {r["path"] for r in recs})):
    for wk in ("pw", "any"):
        for ctl_only in (True, False):
            t = [touch_counts(r, wk, ctl_only) for r in recs if r["path"] in paths]
            t = pd.concat([x for x in t if x is not None])
            go, nogo = t[t.type == "Go"].touches, t[t.type == "Nogo"].touches
            res.append({"recordings": rec_set, "whiskers": wk, "light": "y: without light" if ctl_only else "x: every trial",
                        "go_trials": len(go), "go_mean": go.mean(), "go_sd": go.std(), "nogo_trials": len(nogo), "nogo_mean": nogo.mean(),
                        "nogo_sd": nogo.std()})
res = pd.DataFrame(res)

      "; responses:", pd.Series([x for r in recs for x in r["trials"].response]).value_counts().to_dict())

Result: partially reproduced. Under light reading (x), every trial, with all sessions (b) and the principal whisker (i), mice touched the pole 6.04 times per lick trial (9,794 trials) and 0.85 times per no-lick trial (8,223 trials), both within tolerance of 5.7 and 0.9; no other reading puts both counts within tolerance. Under light reading (y), trials without light only, the same recordings give 5.74 and 0.80, so the no-lick count is outside tolerance and that reading does not match. The trial counts are more than twice the paper's 4,147 and 4,173, so the matching reading is not the paper's set of trials, and no reading gives the paper's trial counts (the nearest, 5,212 and 5,149, come from reading (a) with every trial). Performance during the cortical recordings, now over all 122 cortical cells as in every other group, is 0.681 under (x) and 0.694 under (y), within tolerance of 0.72 (0.703 and 0.718 without the flagged mice, a variant), but during the VPM recordings, which have no light trials, it is 0.585 over 29 units, outside 0.71 +- 0.071.

vpm-touch¶

VPM neurons respond to active touch with a sharp, short-latency increase in spike rate (0.6 +- 0.5 spikes per touch, median 0.4; latency 3.2 +- 1.0 ms, median 2.5 ms).

Result: not reproduced. Over the 29 VPM units, spikes per touch average 0.403 (median 0.268), outside the tolerances of 0.6 and 0.4. The latency median is 2.5 ms with the bin centre (O9 b) and 2.0 ms with its left edge (O9 a) against 2.5 ms, but the mean is 6.14 or 5.64 ms against 3.2, pulled up by one unit at 71.5 ms; 25 units pass the latency exclusion. The files name one principal whisker per file, and 11 of 20 units in files with several whiskers respond most to another one; taking each unit's most responsive whisker, a choice biased upward that the criterion does not make, raises the mean to 0.485, still outside the tolerance.

vpm-whisking¶

VPM neurons fire at 5.1 +- 5.5 spikes/s without whisker movement or touch; most (25 of 29) increase their rate during whisking without touch, and the mean rate rises from 5.1 to 13.5 spikes/s. Three of 29 do not increase with whisking but still respond to touch.

vpm-whisking-phase¶

The spike rate of VPM neurons is modulated by the phase of whisker movement.

Result: reproduced. 25 to 27 of the 29 VPM units have a sinusoid fit of rate against phase with r2 > 0.25 under both filters and every O11 reading, more than half. The measure is weak as a test: with spikes moved to the next trial, 16 of 29 units also pass, which the criterion does not ask for; the units' own spikes pass far more often (25 against 16, and r2 is higher in their own trial, p = 0.0015 in the data check).

exc-vm-touch-whisking¶

In L4 excitatory neurons (37 whole-cell), resting Vm spans -76 to -45 mV (-63 +- 8 mV); every neuron depolarizes after touch (latency 4.8 +- 0.8 ms, amplitude 6.0 +- 2.9 mV), while whisking causes only a small depolarization or hyperpolarization (1.2 +- 2.1 mV).

In [17]:
def vm_table(cls, sel, col="cls", filt="filtfilt", o3="a"):
    paths = group(cls, "whole-cell", sel, col).path
    return vmm[vmm.path.isin(paths) & (vmm.filt == filt) & (vmm.O3 == o3)].set_index("path")

for sel in ("all", "no_flagged"):
    e = vm_table("E", sel)
    pos = e[e.amp_mv > 0]
    print(f"[{sel}] whole-cell E cells: {len(e)} (paper 37); average touch PSP from a median of {int(e.touch_avg_n.median())} touches "
          f"(range {int(e.touch_avg_n.min())} to {int(e.touch_avg_n.max())}); amplitude > 0 in {len(pos)}, latency found in "
          f"{int(pos.latency_ms.notna().sum())} of them")
    print(f"   touch latency (expected mean 4.8 +- 0.48 ms), dVm/dt at the sampling rate (the criterion): mean {e.latency_ms.mean():.2f} "
          f"(s.d. {e.latency_ms.std():.2f}, median {e.latency_ms.median():.2f}, range {e.latency_ms.min():.2f} to {e.latency_ms.max():.2f}); "
          f"for comparison only, 1 ms bins (no longer a reading): left edge mean {e.latency_1ms_edge.mean():.2f}, centre mean "
          f"{e.latency_1ms_centre.mean():.2f}; amplitude mean {e.amp_mv.mean():.2f} mV (expected 6.0 +- 0.6; s.d. {e.amp_mv.std():.2f}, "
          f"median {e.amp_mv.median():.2f}, range {e.amp_mv.min():.2f} to {e.amp_mv.max():.2f})")
    print(f"   resting Vm O4a mean {e.rest_mean.mean():.2f} mV (s.d. {e.rest_mean.std():.2f}, range {e.rest_mean.min():.1f} to "
          f"{e.rest_mean.max():.1f}); O4b (median per cell) mean {e.rest_median.mean():.2f} (expected -63 +- 6.3)")
    for filt in yu2016.FILTERS:
        ef = vm_table("E", sel, filt=filt)
        print(f"   {filt}, earlier rule of this attempt (epochs O11 a-i, 250 ms rule on principal-whisker touches): whisking change (a) onset windows mean {ef.whisk_onset_change.mean():.2f} mV (s.d. {ef.whisk_onset_change.std():.2f}; "
              f"cells with onsets {int(ef.whisk_onset_change.notna().sum())}, onsets per cell median {int(ef.n_onsets.median())}); "

      .round(2).reset_index(drop=True).to_dict("records"))

# Whisking onsets and epochs under readings O10 (windows of the 2 degree rise: a, Supp. Fig. 4 windows; b, 0 to 250 ms
# after against the whole nonwhisking period) and O11 (touches bounding epochs and onsets: a, every tracked whisker;
# b, the principal whisker; i, 10 ms before onset to 100 ms after offset; ii, to 100 ms after onset). Answer of 2026-10-20.
o_rows = []
for cls_, p in [("E", p) for p in group("E", "whole-cell").path] + [("FS", p) for p in group("FS", "whole-cell").path]:
    r = by_path[p]
    m = ctl_mask(r)
    vm = r["vm1k"].astype(float)
    tri = r["beh"]["trial"]
    use = (tri >= 0) & m[np.clip(tri, 0, None)] & np.isfinite(vm)
    for filt in yu2016.FILTERS:
        for (o10, o11) in r["beh"][filt]["readings"]:
            e_ = yu2016.beh_reading(r["beh"], filt, o10, o11)[filt]
            res_, pre_, d_ = yu2016.vm_epoch_measures(vm, use, e_)
            o_rows.append({"cls": cls_, "path": p, "subject": r["subject"], "filter": filt, "O10": o10, "O11": o11, **res_,
                           "whisk_pre": np.array(pre_), "whisk_dvm": np.array(d_)})
ovm_all = pd.DataFrame(o_rows)
ovm = ovm_all[ovm_all.cls == "E"]
rows = []
for sel in ("all", "no_flagged"):
    g0 = ovm if sel == "all" else ovm[~ovm.subject.isin(flagged)]
    for (filt, o10, o11), g in g0.groupby(["filter", "O10", "O11"]):
        rows.append({"cells": sel, "filter": filt, "O10": o10, "O11": o11, "n": len(g), "rest_O4a": g.rest_mean.mean(),
                     "rest_O4b": g.rest_median.mean(), "onset_cells": int(g.whisk_onset_change.notna().sum()),

                     "whisk_change_a_sd": g.whisk_onset_change.std(), "whisk_change_b_epochs": g.whisk_epoch_change.mean(),
                     "a_within": within(g.whisk_onset_change.mean(), 1.2, 0.35), "b_within": within(g.whisk_epoch_change.mean(), 1.2, 0.35),
                     "rest_within": within(g.rest_mean.mean(), -63, 6.3)})
oread = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nWhisking change and resting Vm of the whole-cell E cells under readings O10 and O11 (expected whisking change 1.2 +- 0.35 mV, "

Range over readings (all cells): whisking change (a) 0.65 to 0.87 mV, (b) 1.08 to 1.14 mV; resting Vm (O4 a) -61.69 to -61.66 mV

Result: partially reproduced. Every one of the 48 whole-cell excitatory cells with enough touches depolarizes after touch and has a latency (3 cells have fewer than 5 touches). Resting Vm (mean -61.69 mV, or -61.89 with the median per cell) is within tolerance under every reading, but the touch amplitude (4.78 mV against 6.0 +- 0.6) and the latency (mean 7.68 ms with dVm/dt at the sampling rate, median 4.90, against 4.8 +- 0.48) are not, and neither depends on the whisking readings. The latency diagnostic below shows that the criterion's rule picks single-sample excursions of dVm/dt in 5 cells (under 1 ms) and is pulled up by late crossings in others (up to 101 ms). Under the 16 combinations of readings O10, O11 and the two filters, the whisking change with the onset windows ranges from 0.65 to 0.87 mV and is within 1.2 +- 0.35 in 2 (zero-phase filter, O10 a, O11 b-i and b-ii, 0.87 and 0.86 mV); with the epochs it is 1.08 to 1.14 mV and within tolerance in all 16. The group holds 51 cells against the paper's 37 and includes the 8 cells of the flagged mice; without them the amplitude is 5.54 mV and the latency 4.97 ms, both within tolerance, but that variant does not decide. Amplitudes go down to 0.01 mV: the peak of the average minus the pre-touch mean is positive for nearly any average, so "every neuron depolarizes" is a weak test.

exc-threshold-touch-vs-whisking¶

Touch moves the membrane potential of L4 excitatory neurons much closer to spike threshold than whisking does (shift 6.1 +- 3.2 mV against 1.1 +- 2.0 mV).

Result: partially reproduced. Touch moves the 50 excitatory cells closer to threshold than whisking does in 43 or 44 of them under every filter and O11 reading (signed-rank p = 9e-11 to 1.3e-10). The touch shift averages 4.60 to 4.67 mV, outside the tolerance of 6.1 +- 0.61, and the whisking shift 0.84 to 1.16 mV, within 1.1 +- 0.33 under every reading. The two threshold readings O3 give the same values: a cell's median threshold differs by at most 0.0089 mV and 8 of 41,620 spikes change threshold, since a trial's mean dVm/dt is close to zero. 17 of the 50 cells fire no spike, so their threshold is the default -42 mV.

exc-effective-reversal¶

The effective reversal potential of the touch response of L4 excitatory neurons is more depolarized than resting Vm, while that of whisking is close to rest and more hyperpolarized than that of touch.

In [19]:

        rw = e.apply(lambda x: yu2016.reversal(x.whisk_pre, x.whisk_dvm)[0], axis=1)

Result: reproduced. Fitted per neuron, the touch reversal (median -50.0 mV) lies above the whisking reversal (median -57.4 to -60.9 mV over the filters and the O10 and O11 readings) in 38 to 40 of 47 or 48 neurons and above the median resting Vm (-63.9 mV); one pooled fit per event type gives -31.90 mV for touch and -51.6 to -56.3 mV for whisking, both above rest as well. The median of exactly -50.00 mV is the mean of the two middle neurons, -50.231 and -49.769 mV.

fs-touch-response¶

L4 FS interneurons fire at 9.3 +- 8.5 spikes/s without whisker movement and fire 1.9 +- 1.0 spikes per touch, with a spike latency of 5.3 +- 2.1 ms.

In [20]:
# FS readings of the criterion (answer of 2026-10-20): driven at (a) p < 0.001 or (b) p < 0.01, each (i) with or
# (ii) without the approximate waveform boundary. The paper's counts are the check: 19 ChR2-tagged control FS cells
# (5 whole-cell, 14 cell-attached), and 14 control plus 10 ION-cut cell-attached FS cells in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice.
cnt = []

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). The FS readings of the criterion give different outcomes. With the boundary, (a)(i) and (b)(i) give the same 17 cells with a principal whisker (the paper has 26): the nonwhisking rate (8.53 spikes/s; 8.52 to 8.72 over the O11 readings and filters) and the latency (5.23 ms with the bin edge, 5.73 ms with the centre, over 13 cells) are within tolerance and spikes per touch (1.50) is not, so two of three values match (partially reproduced). Without the boundary, (a)(ii) has 25 cells and (b)(ii) 28, with 1.48 and 1.39 spikes per touch and latencies of 6.16 to 6.66 and 10.64 to 11.14 ms, so only the nonwhisking rate is within tolerance (not reproduced). Against the paper's counts, the dandiset's VGAT-ChR2 mice give 4 whole-cell FS cells (paper 5) under every reading, and 12, 20, 12 and 23 cell-attached FS cells under (a)(i), (a)(ii), (b)(i) and (b)(ii), against 24 (14 control and 10 ION-cut), so the readings without the boundary come closer to the paper's count. Spikes per touch is 1.39 to 1.50 under every reading, below 1.9 +- 0.2.

fs-vm-touch-whisking¶

In whole-cell L4 FS interneurons (n = 7), touch depolarizes the membrane by 7.0 +- 5.2 mV with onset 4.0 +- 0.6 ms, and whisking depolarizes it by 2.7 +- 2.1 mV toward threshold.

# Cause of the near-zero Vm latencies (the verifier's request). For each whole-cell E and FS cell, the touch-aligned average
# (full rate) and its first difference dVm/dt, with the criterion's threshold (3 s.d. of dVm/dt 0 to 25 ms before onset). Also,
# as a diagnostic that decides nothing, the latency with the baseline's mean dVm/dt subtracted before the comparison.
def lat_diag(rec):
    fs = rec["vm_hz"]
    a = rec["touch_avg"].astype(float)
    i0 = int(yu2016.EVENT_PRE_S * fs)
    d = np.diff(a) * fs / 1000.0
    base = d[i0 - int(0.025 * fs):i0]
    thr = 3 * base.std()
    hit = np.flatnonzero(d[i0:] > thr)
    hit_m = np.flatnonzero(d[i0:] - base.mean() > thr)
    pre = a[i0 - int(0.005 * fs):i0].mean()
    return {"fs": fs, "base_mean": base.mean(), "base_sd": base.std(), "thr": thr, "d_first_0.5ms_max": d[i0:i0 + int(0.0005 * fs)].max(),
            "latency_ms": hit[0] / fs * 1000 if len(hit) else np.nan, "latency_mean_subtracted_ms": hit_m[0] / fs * 1000 if len(hit_m) else np.nan,
            "vm_0_to_1ms_minus_pre": a[i0:i0 + int(0.001 * fs)].mean() - pre, "d": d, "a": a - pre, "i0": i0}
ld = []
for cls_ in ("E", "FS"):
    for p in group(cls_, "whole-cell").path:
        r = by_path[p]
        if r.get("touch_avg") is None or r["touch_avg_n"] < 5:
            continue
        x = lat_diag(r)
        ld.append({"cls": cls_, "path": p, "subject": r["subject"], "touches": r["touch_avg_n"], **{k: v for k, v in x.items() if np.ndim(v) == 0}})
ld = pd.DataFrame(ld)
print("Cells with the criterion's latency under 2 ms:")
print(ld[ld.latency_ms < 2].drop(columns="path").round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("All cells: dVm/dt baseline mean against its s.d., median ratio", round(float((ld.base_mean / ld.base_sd).median()), 3))
for cls_, g in ld.groupby("cls"):
    print(f"{cls_}: {len(g)} cells; latency mean {g.latency_ms.mean():.2f} ms (median {g.latency_ms.median():.2f}); under 1 ms {int((g.latency_ms < 1).sum())}; "
          f"diagnostic with the baseline mean subtracted, mean {g.latency_mean_subtracted_ms.mean():.2f} ms")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, max(1, int((ld.latency_ms < 2).sum())), figsize=(2.4 * max(1, int((ld.latency_ms < 2).sum())), 4), squeeze=False)
for j, p in enumerate(ld[ld.latency_ms < 2].path):
    x = lat_diag(by_path[p])
    fs, i0 = x["fs"], x["i0"]
    sl = slice(i0 - int(0.002 * fs), i0 + int(0.002 * fs))
    tms = (np.arange(len(x["a"]))[sl] - i0) / fs * 1000
    ax[0, j].plot(tms, x["a"][sl], color="k", lw=0.8); ax[0, j].axvline(0, color="C0", lw=0.5)
    ax[0, j].set_title(by_path[p]["subject"], fontsize=7)
    ax[1, j].plot(tms, x["d"][sl], color="k", lw=0.8); ax[1, j].axhline(x["thr"], color="C3", lw=0.6); ax[1, j].axvline(0, color="C0", lw=0.5)
    ax[1, j].set_xlabel("ms from touch onset", fontsize=7)
    print(f"{by_path[p]['subject']} ({ld.set_index('path').cls[p]}): Vm minus pre (mV) -2 to +2 ms, every 0.2 ms:",
          np.round(x["a"][sl][::max(1, int(fs // 5000))], 3).tolist())
    print("   dVm/dt (mV/ms), same samples:", np.round(x["d"][sl][::max(1, int(fs // 5000))], 2).tolist(), "; threshold", round(x["thr"], 2))
ax[0, 0].set_ylabel("Vm - pre (mV)"); ax[1, 0].set_ylabel("dVm/dt (mV/ms)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("Each panel shows -2 to +2 ms; every plotted value lies within the axes.")

Each panel shows -2 to +2 ms; every plotted value lies within the axes.

The latencies under 2 ms in E and FS cells come from single samples of dVm/dt, at 10 or 20 kHz, that just cross 3 s.d. of the baseline before any sustained rise; the Vm of the E cells is within 0.17 mV of its pre-touch mean in the first millisecond (the values above). A 3 s.d. threshold on an unsmoothed derivative is crossed by single samples of noise; in the laser-onset averages of exc-thalamus-photoinhibition 1 and 3 of the 250 baseline samples already cross it. This is the rule the criterion fixes (O8, answer of 2026-10-20), so the latencies stand as measured; the diagnostic decides nothing.

Result: not reproduced. The dandiset holds 5 whole-cell FS cells by the claims file's rules (the paper has 7). Their touch amplitude averages 5.56 mV (within 7.0 +- 1.97) and the whisking depolarization 2.54 mV with the onset windows (within 2.7 +- 0.79; 1.47 to 2.55 mV over the O10 and O11 readings, within tolerance in 12 of 16; 1.01 mV with the threshold distance), but the touch latency, with dVm/dt at the sampling rate as the criterion says, averages 1.88 ms (median 1.35) against 4.0 +- 0.4. The latency diagnostic above (after exc-vm-touch-whisking) shows why: in anm220466 (0.00 ms) and anm220470 (0.30 ms) the first crossing is a single sample of dVm/dt just above the threshold (0.96 against 0.71 and 3.05 against 1.85 mV/ms), in averages whose Vm already lies 0.26 to 0.46 mV above its pre-touch mean at onset. Subtracting the baseline's mean dVm/dt, a diagnostic that decides nothing, does not move these crossings (mean 1.76 ms), so the rule as the criterion gives it, not an offset, yields these latencies.

fs-whisking-rate¶

Most L4 FS interneurons (23 of 26) increase their spike rate during whisking without touch and 3 of 26 decrease it; over the population the rate roughly doubles (to 21.1 +- 15.8 spikes/s).

In [23]:
def fs_rate_table(groups):
    rows = []
    for rname, col in groups.items():
        for sel in ("all", "no_flagged"):
            g = group("FS", None, sel, col)
            for f in yu2016.FILTERS:
                for o2 in ("O2a", "O2b"):
                    rows.append({"FS reading": rname, "cells": sel, "filter": f, "samples": o2, "n": len(g),
                                 "increase": int((g[f"{f}:{o2}"] == 1).sum()), "decrease": int((g[f"{f}:{o2}"] == -1).sum()),
                                 "nonwhisk_mean": g[f"{f}:rate_nonwhisk"].mean(), "whisk_mean": g[f"{f}:rate_whisk"].mean(),
                                 "whisk_sd": g[f"{f}:rate_whisk"].std(), "whisk_median": g[f"{f}:rate_whisk"].median(),
                                 "signed_rank_p": "%.2g" % wilcox(g[f"{f}:rate_nonwhisk"], g[f"{f}:rate_whisk"])})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

The 17 FS cells fire more during whisking under every filter, sample and O11 reading (signed-rank p = 0.0002 to 0.0005), with a mean whisking rate of 17.77 to 19.17 spikes/s (within 21.1 +- 3.1 with the zero-phase filter; outside with the forward one). 13 or 14 cells increase and 1 to 3 decrease significantly against the paper's 23 and 3 of 26, so the increase count is outside its tolerance under every reading; the group is smaller than the paper's.

fs-touch-and-whisking¶

Touch- and whisking-evoked spikes are typically multiplexed in individual L4 FS neurons, as in VPM neurons.

exc-mainly-touch¶

L4 excitatory neurons respond mostly to touch (0.3 +- 0.4 spikes per touch, n = 85) and only weakly to whisker movement; their rate does not change significantly between nonwhisking and whisking (0.4 to 0.6 spikes/s, P = 0.20).

Rates by mode (filtfilt), means: {'cell-attached': {'spt': 0.534, 'filtfilt:rate_nonwhisk': 2.451, 'filtfilt:rate_whisk': 6.193}, 'whole-cell': {'spt': 0.122, 'filtfilt:rate_nonwhisk': 0.698, 'filtfilt:rate_whisk': 1.168}}

Result: not reproduced. The 97 excitatory cells fire more during whisking than without it under every filter and O11 reading (signed-rank p = 9.1e-07 for the main epochs, at most 8.7e-06 for the forward filter), so the paper's absence of a change is not found. Spikes per touch (0.320) is within tolerance of 0.3, but the nonwhisking (1.53 to 1.59 spikes/s) and whisking (3.38 to 3.64) rates are well above 0.4 and 0.6; the 46 cell-attached cells fire more than the 51 whole-cell ones (2.45 against 0.70 spikes/s without whisking). The data check shows that double detection removes only 8.1% of the cell-attached spikes, so it does not explain the high rates.

Light experiments¶

The functions below select the light trials and the windows used by the thalamic photoinhibition and PV suppression claims (windows O5, fractions O6, laser powers O7).

In [27]:
# Light designs. Thalamic photoinhibition: trials lit at the site labelled VPM and at no other site (VGAT-ChR2 mice).
# PV suppression: trials lit at the vS1 site of PV-IRES-Cre mice (constant light). Control trials have no light at
# any site. Windows O5: (a) control samples inside the median light span of the lit trials, (b) anywhere.
def light_design(r, region):
    tr = r["trials"]
    sites = [s for s, L in r["light"].items() if L["region"] == region and len(L["pulses"])]
    if not sites:
        return None
    s = sites[0]
    w = yu2016.light_windows(r["light"], s, tr)
    other = set()
    for s2 in r["light"]:
        if s2 != s:
            other |= set(yu2016.light_windows(r["light"], s2, tr).trial.astype(int))
    w = w[~w.trial.isin(other)]
    if len(w) == 0:
        return None
    P = r["light"][s]["pulses"]
    pk = yu2016.per_trial_index(P[:, 0], tr)
    pw = r["light"][s].get("pulse_power", np.ones(len(P)))
    power = {int(t): float(pw[pk == t].max()) for t in w.trial}
    return {"site": s, "windows": {int(t): (a, b) for t, a, b in zip(w.trial, w.rel_start, w.rel_stop)},
            "span": (float(w.rel_start.median()), float(w.rel_stop.median())), "power": power,
            "ctl": ~yu2016.lit_trials(r["light"], tr)}

def masks(r, d, reading, top_power=False):
    b, tr = r["beh"], r["trials"]
    tri = b["trial"]
    rel = b["t"] - tr.start.to_numpy()[np.clip(tri, 0, None)]
    lo, hi = np.full(len(tr), np.inf), np.full(len(tr), -np.inf)
    pmax = max(d["power"].values())
    for t, (a, c) in d["windows"].items():
        if not top_power or d["power"][t] == pmax:
            lo[t], hi[t] = a, c
    k = np.clip(tri, 0, None)
    use_l = (tri >= 0) & (rel >= lo[k]) & (rel < hi[k])
    use_c = (tri >= 0) & d["ctl"][k]
    if reading == "a":
        use_c &= (rel >= d["span"][0]) & (rel < d["span"][1])
    return use_l, use_c

def light_compare(r, spikes, d, filt="filtfilt", reading="a", definition="cortex5", min_iti=0.025, top_power=False, o11="a-i"):
    b = r["beh"] if o11 == "a-i" else yu2016.beh_o11(r["beh"], o11)
    use_l, use_c = masks(r, d, reading, top_power)
    count = yu2016.counts_1k(spikes, b)
    out = {}
    on = yu2016.touches(b, None, min_iti)
    for tag, u in (("light", use_l), ("ctl", use_c)):
        er = yu2016.epoch_rates(np.where(u, count, 0), b, filt, u)
        out[f"{tag}_nonwhisk"], out[f"{tag}_whisk"] = er["rate_nonwhisk"], er["rate_whisk"]
        out[f"{tag}_t_nonwhisk"], out[f"{tag}_t_whisk"] = er["time_nonwhisk"], er["time_whisk"]
        s = yu2016.spikes_per_touch(count, b["trial"], on[u[on]], definition)
        out[f"{tag}_spt"], out[f"{tag}_touches"] = s["spt"], s["n_touches"]
        out[f"{tag}_rate"] = count[u].sum() / max(u.sum(), 1) * 1000
    return out

def frac(light, ctl, how):
    light, ctl = np.asarray(light, float), np.asarray(ctl, float)
    ok = np.isfinite(light) & np.isfinite(ctl)
    if how == "a":
        return light[ok].mean() / ctl[ok].mean()
    ok &= ctl > 0
    return float(np.median(light[ok] / ctl[ok]))

thalamus-drives-fs¶

Photoinhibiting the thalamus reduces the spike rates of L4 FS interneurons during nonwhisking (to 4% of control), whisking (to 13%) and touch (to 32%), so FS interneurons are driven by thalamic input.

In [28]:
def thal_rows(col):
    out = []
    for r in l4:
        c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
        if c[col] != "FS" or c.line != "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP" or r["beh"]["principal"] is None:
            continue
        d = light_design(r, "VPM")
        if d is None:
            continue
        for filt in yu2016.FILTERS:
            for reading in ("a", "b"):
                for top in (False, True):
                    for o11 in yu2016.O11:
                        out.append({"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "filter": filt, "O5": reading, "O7": "b" if top else "a",
                                    "O11": o11, "lit_trials": len(d["windows"]), "powers": sorted(set(d["power"].values())),
                                    **light_compare(r, r["spikes"], d, filt, reading, top_power=top, o11=o11)})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

def thal_summary(t):
    rows = []
    for (filt, o5, o7, o11), g in t.groupby(["filter", "O5", "O7", "O11"]):
        row = {"filter": filt, "O5": o5, "O7": o7, "O11": o11, "cells": len(g)}
        for m in ("nonwhisk", "whisk", "spt"):
            gg = g.dropna(subset=[f"light_{m}", f"ctl_{m}"])
            row.update({f"{m}_n": len(gg), f"{m}_O6a": frac(gg[f"light_{m}"], gg[f"ctl_{m}"], "a"),
                        f"{m}_O6b": frac(gg[f"light_{m}"], gg[f"ctl_{m}"], "b"),
                        f"{m}_lower": int((gg[f"light_{m}"] < gg[f"ctl_{m}"]).sum()), f"{m}_p": "%.2g" % wilcox(gg[f"light_{m}"], gg[f"ctl_{m}"]),
                        f"{m}_p_one_sided": "%.2g" % wilcox(gg[f"light_{m}"], gg[f"ctl_{m}"], "less")})
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: blocked (too few cells). Only 5 FS cells by the claims file's rule were recorded with thalamic light, all from one mouse (anm260070), and with 5 cells a two-sided signed-rank test, which the criterion names, cannot reach p < 0.05 (smallest p 0.0625; 0.062 to 0.12 over every reading here). The rates fall with the light in all 5 cells without whisking and in 4 of 5 during whisking, to 0.20 and 0.27 of control (population means, all powers, main epochs), and spikes per touch to 0.41; at the highest power only the nonwhisking rate falls to 0.022 of control. Over the 32 combinations of filter, window, power and O11 reading the fractions are 0 to 0.32 without whisking and 0.15 to 0.29 with it, above the paper's 0.13 for whisking under every reading. The one-sided variant, which does not decide, gives p = 0.031 for the nonwhisking rate and spikes per touch and 0.062 for the whisking rate. The variant without the waveform boundary (9 cells) passes all three two-sided tests (p = 0.012, 0.0078 and 0.0039) with fractions of 0.20, 0.29 and 0.46, outside tolerance, so the best it could give is partially reproduced.

exc-thalamus-photoinhibition¶

Thalamic photoinhibition hyperpolarizes L4 excitatory neurons and reduces their Vm fluctuations, with an onset latency of 4.2 ms, longer than the 2.8 ms latency of direct cortical GABAergic activation.

In [29]:
from scipy import signal as sg
bh, ah = sg.butter(2, 10 / 500, "high")
def vm_light(r, d, reading):
    b = r["beh"]
    use_l, use_c = masks(r, d, reading)
    vm = r["vm1k"].astype(float)
    hp = np.full(len(vm), np.nan)
    for k in np.unique(b["trial"][b["trial"] >= 0]):
        i = np.flatnonzero(b["trial"] == k)
        x = vm[i]
        g = np.isfinite(x)
        if g.sum() > 100:
            hp[i] = sg.filtfilt(bh, ah, np.interp(np.arange(len(x)), np.flatnonzero(g), x[g]))
            hp[i[~g]] = np.nan
    keep = ~b["excl"] & np.isfinite(vm)
    return {f"{t}_{q}": f(x[u & keep]) for t, u in (("light", use_l), ("ctl", use_c)) for q, x, f in (("vm", vm, np.mean), ("var", hp, np.nanvar))}

def resample(avg, fs):
    """20 kHz averages to 10 kHz by the mean of each pair of samples (an anti-alias step before decimation)."""
    k = int(fs // 10000)
    return avg if k == 1 else avg[: len(avg) // k * k].reshape(-1, k).mean(axis=1)

rows, avgs = [], []
for r in l4:
    c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
    if c.cls != "E" or r["mode"] != "whole-cell" or c.line != "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP" or "vm1k" not in r:
        continue
    d = light_design(r, "VPM")
    if d is None:
        continue
    for reading in ("a", "b"):
        rows.append({"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "O5": reading, "lit_trials": len(d["windows"]), **vm_light(r, d, reading)})
    la = r["light_avg"].get(d["site"], {}).get("first", (None, 0))
    if la[0] is not None:
        avgs.append(resample(la[0], r["vm_hz"]) - resample(la[0], r["vm_hz"])[:int(0.05 * 10000)].mean())
tp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Whole-cell E cells with thalamic light:", tp.path.nunique(), "(paper 12), from", tp.subject.nunique(), "mice; lit trials per cell",
      tp.drop_duplicates("path").lit_trials.tolist())
for reading, g in tp.groupby("O5"):
    print(f"O5 {reading}: Vm lower with light in {(g.light_vm < g.ctl_vm).sum()} of {len(g)} (median change {np.median(g.light_vm - g.ctl_vm):.2f} mV, "
          f"signed-rank p = {wilcox(g.light_vm, g.ctl_vm):.2g}); variance (>10 Hz) lower in {(g.light_var < g.ctl_var).sum()} "
          f"(median ratio {np.median(g.light_var / g.ctl_var):.2f}, p = {wilcox(g.light_var, g.ctl_var):.2g})")
ga = np.mean(avgs, axis=0) if avgs else None
lat_thal = yu2016.neg_onset_latency(ga, len(avgs), 10000)
lat_thal_1ms = yu2016.neg_onset_latency(ga, len(avgs), 10000, binned=True)
print(f"Grand average aligned to thalamic laser onset ({len(avgs)} cells): onset latency of the hyperpolarization {lat_thal:.2f} ms at the sampling rate "
      f"(the criterion; expected 4.2 +- 0.42); for comparison only, {lat_thal_1ms:.1f} ms in 1 ms bins (no longer a reading); "
      f"mean change 10 to 50 ms after onset {ga[int(0.06 * 1e4):int(0.1 * 1e4)].mean():.2f} mV")
cav = []
for r in l4:
    c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
    if c.cls != "E" or r["mode"] != "whole-cell" or c.line != "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP" or "vm1k" not in r:
        continue
    for s, L in r["light"].items():
        if "vS1" in L["region"]:
            a, n = r["light_avg"].get(s, {}).get("isolated", (None, 0))
            if a is not None and n >= 5:
                x = resample(a, r["vm_hz"])
                cav.append(x - x[:int(0.05 * 1e4)].mean())
gc = np.mean(cav, axis=0) if cav else None

# The 0.1 ms laser latencies (the verifier's request): the grand averages -2 to +2 ms from laser onset, their first difference
# and the criterion's threshold (3 s.d. of the first difference 0 to 25 ms before onset, turned downward), at 10 kHz.
for name, avg_ in (("thalamic light", ga), ("cortical tag pulses", gc)):
    avg_ = np.asarray(avg_, float)
    i0 = int(0.05 * 1e4)
    d = np.diff(avg_)                    # d[i] is the change into sample i + 1
    base = d[i0 - 251:i0 - 1]
    thr = 3 * base.std()
    hit = np.flatnonzero(d[i0 - 1:] < -thr)
    print(f"{name}: Vm (mV) -2 to +2 ms in 0.1 ms steps:", np.round(avg_[i0 - 20:i0 + 21], 3).tolist())
    print("   first difference (mV per 0.1 ms) into each of those samples:", np.round(d[i0 - 21:i0 + 20], 4).tolist(), "; threshold", round(-thr, 4))
    print(f"   baseline samples beyond the threshold: {int(np.sum(base < -thr))} of {len(base)}; first sample beyond it after onset "
          f"{hit[0] / 10:.1f} ms, a change of {d[i0 - 1 + hit[0]]:.4f} mV; step across onset (mean 0 to 1 ms minus mean -1 to 0 ms) "
          f"{avg_[i0:i0 + 10].mean() - avg_[i0 - 10:i0].mean():.3f} mV")
    later = hit[hit >= 20]
    print(f"   first sample beyond it 2 ms or more after onset (diagnostic, decides nothing): {later[0] / 10 if len(later) else np.nan:.1f} ms")

Result: partially reproduced. Thalamic light hyperpolarizes 12 of 13 whole-cell excitatory cells (median -4.02 mV) and lowers their Vm variance above 10 Hz in 10 (median ratio 0.55), under both window readings. With dVm/dt at the sampling rate, as the criterion says, the onset latency is 0.10 ms for both the thalamic light (13 cells) and the cortical tag pulses (14 cells, now that every pulse of a train counts), against 4.2 and 2.8 ms, so the thalamic latency is not longer. The diagnostic above shows the cause: one sample 0.1 ms after light onset drops by 0.061 mV (thalamic) and 0.064 mV (cortical) and the next sample returns, a one-sample transient at light onset, likely an artifact, which crosses the threshold. The first crossing 2 ms or more after onset, a diagnostic that decides nothing, is at 4.9 ms (thalamic) and 5.2 ms (cortical), but the two thresholds differ (-0.0206 and -0.0557 mV per sample; 1 and 3 of the 250 baseline samples already cross them), so this does not compare the two latencies. The other outputs above put the thalamic onset later: 5.0 against 3.0 ms in 1 ms bins, and in 0.5 ms steps the thalamic average starts to fall at about 4.5 to 5 ms and the cortical one at about 3 ms. None of these is the criterion's rule, so they decide nothing; by the rule the thalamic latency is not longer. The 20 kHz averages are now brought to 10 kHz by averaging pairs of samples.

pv-enphr-suppression¶

Yellow light in PV-IRES-Cre mice expressing eNpHR3.0 strongly inhibits most L4 PV interneurons (3 of 4); their rate falls 3 ms after laser onset and L4 excitatory activity rises 2 ms later.

In [31]:
def boot_rate_ci(count, b, filt, use, rng):
    """95% bootstrap interval (1,000 draws over trials) of the rate in nonwhisking and whisking samples."""
    out = {}
    tri = b["trial"]
    for name in ("nonwhisk", "whisk"):
        m = b[filt][name] & use & (tri >= 0)
        ks = tri[m]
        n = tri.max() + 1
        c = np.bincount(ks, weights=count[m], minlength=n)
        t = np.bincount(ks, minlength=n) / 1000
        keep = t > 0
        c, t = c[keep], t[keep]
        if len(c) < 2:
            out[name] = (np.nan, np.nan)
            continue
        idx = rng.integers(0, len(c), (yu2016.N_BOOT, len(c)))
        bs = c[idx].sum(axis=1) / t[idx].sum(axis=1)
        out[name] = (np.percentile(bs, 2.5), np.percentile(bs, 97.5))
    return out

def onset_psth(r, d):
    """Rate (spikes/s) in 1 ms bins from 25 ms before to 100 ms after the first light sample of each lit trial."""
    sp = np.sort(r["spikes"])
    st = r["trials"].start.to_numpy()
    on = np.array([st[t] + w[0] for t, w in d["windows"].items()])
    edges = np.arange(-25, 101) / 1000
    h = np.zeros(len(edges) - 1)
    for o in on:
        h += np.histogram(sp[(sp >= o - 0.025) & (sp < o + 0.1)] - o, edges)[0]
    return h / len(on) * 1000

def psth_crossing(m, sign):
    lags = np.arange(-25, 100)
    dd = np.diff(m)
    lag_d = lags[1:]
    thr = 3 * dd[(lag_d >= -25) & (lag_d < 0)].std()
    hit = np.flatnonzero((lag_d >= 0) & (sign * dd > thr))
    return (float(lag_d[hit[0]]), float(lag_d[hit[0]] + 0.5)) if len(hit) else (np.nan, np.nan)

rng = np.random.default_rng(13)
rows, ps_pv, ps_e = [], [], []
for r in l4:
    c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
    if c.line != "PV-IRES-Cre" or r["beh"]["principal"] is None:
        continue
    d = light_design(r, "vS1")
    if d is None:
        continue
    ps = onset_psth(r, d)
    if c.cls == "FS":

Result: partially reproduced. 3 PV cells are identified by their inactivation, and all 3 are strongly inhibited (their light rate below the control interval in both periods); the paper's fourth PV cell cannot be found. Since the cells are found by their inactivation, the count cannot fail, and a fourth PV cell that the light did not inhibit would be classed excitatory. The parts that could fail fail: the dPSTH/dt rule finds no fall in the grand average of the 3 PV cells, and the excitatory cells' rise is found at 48.0 ms with the bin edge (O9 a) and 48.5 ms with its centre (O9 b), so neither latency is within tolerance under either bin position.

fs-suppress-movement-spiking¶

Partially suppressing PV (FS) interneurons increases the spike rate of L4 excitatory neurons during nonwhisking (0.6 to 1.6 spikes/s) and whisking (0.8 to 2.7 spikes/s).

In [32]:
def pv_rows(min_iti=0.025, definition="cortex5", o11s=yu2016.O11):
    out = []
    for r in l4:
        c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
        if c.line != "PV-IRES-Cre" or c.cls != "E" or r["beh"]["principal"] is None:
            continue
        d = light_design(r, "vS1")
        if d is None:
            continue
        for filt in yu2016.FILTERS:
            for reading in ("a", "b"):
                for o11 in o11s:
                    out.append({"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "mode": r["mode"], "filter": filt, "O5": reading, "O11": o11,
                                "lit_trials": len(d["windows"]), **light_compare(r, r["spikes"], d, filt, reading, definition, min_iti, o11=o11)})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

Result: partially reproduced. In the 42 excitatory cells of PV-IRES-Cre mice the light raises the nonwhisking rate (32 to 36 cells, p at most 7.4e-05) and the whisking rate (31 to 34 cells, p at most 0.0003) under every filter, window and O11 reading, but the rates are higher than the paper's: 1.18 to 1.32 rising to 2.26 to 2.55 spikes/s without whisking (paper 0.6 to 1.6) and 3.36 to 4.31 rising to 5.69 to 6.63 with it (paper 0.8 to 2.7), outside the tolerances. Most of these cells are cell-attached (34 of 42), whose rates are high throughout this dandiset (data check).

fs-enhance-touch-selectivity¶

With PV interneurons suppressed, L4 excitatory neurons become driven by whisker movement (whisking rate above nonwhisking, P = 0.02), while in control trials they are not (P = 0.55); their selectivity for touch is normally maintained in part by FS interneurons.

Ranges over the 16 readings: p with light (1.7e-06, 3.7e-05) ; p in control trials (6.7e-06, 0.00013)

Result: partially reproduced. With the light, whisking rates exceed nonwhisking rates in 31 to 33 of 42 cells (p = 1.7e-06 to 3.7e-05 over the 16 readings), as the paper reports, but in control trials they do too (27 to 35 of 42, p = 6.7e-06 to 0.00013), where the paper found no difference (P = 0.55).

exc-touch-spikes-enphr¶

PV interneuron suppression does not change mean touch-evoked spiking of L4 excitatory neurons significantly (0.27 to 0.32 spikes per touch, P = 0.09); its effect is heterogeneous, with weakly responding neurons responding more and strongly responding neurons unchanged or less.

auc-weak-strong¶

Suppressing PV interneurons improves touch detection (AUC) for L4 excitatory neurons with weak touch responses and diminishes it for neurons with robust touch responses.

In [35]:
def auc_inputs(r, d, rng, reading):
    """Per trial, spike counts in the 250 ms before and after the first principal-whisker touch, or (no touch) in two
    adjacent 250 ms windows of the sample epoch: reading (a) at a random time, (b) around the median first-touch time
    of the touch trials. Light trials count when the 500 ms lie inside the light."""
    b, tr = r["beh"], r["trials"]
    sp = np.sort(r["spikes"])
    st = tr.start.to_numpy()
    on_t = b["t"][b["touch_on"]]
    k = yu2016.per_trial_index(on_t, tr)
    first = {}
    for t, kk in zip(on_t, k):
        if kk >= 0 and kk not in first:
            first[kk] = t
    med = np.median([first[kk] - st[kk] for kk in first]) if first else np.nan
    out = {"ctl": {"t": [[], []], "n": [[], []]}, "light": {"t": [[], []], "n": [[], []]}}
    cnt = lambda a, z: int(np.searchsorted(sp, z) - np.searchsorted(sp, a))
    for kk in range(len(tr)):
        if d["ctl"][kk]:
            cond, win = "ctl", None
        elif kk in d["windows"]:
            cond, win = "light", d["windows"][kk]
        else:
            continue
        if kk in first:
            t0, key = first[kk], "t"
        else:
            p0, p1 = tr.pole_in_time.iloc[kk], tr.pole_out_time.iloc[kk]
            if not (np.isfinite(p0) and np.isfinite(p1)) or p1 - p0 < 0.5:
                continue
            t0 = rng.uniform(p0 + 0.25, p1 - 0.25) if reading == "a" else st[kk] + med
            key = "n"
        if win is not None and not (st[kk] + win[0] <= t0 - 0.25 and t0 + 0.25 <= st[kk] + win[1]):
            continue
        if t0 - 0.25 < st[kk] or t0 + 0.25 > st[kk] + yu2016.ANALYSIS_END_S:
            continue
        out[cond][key][0].append(cnt(t0 - 0.25, t0))
        out[cond][key][1].append(cnt(t0, t0 + 0.25))
    return out

def auc_table(reading, rng):
    rows_ = []
    for r in l4:
        c = cells.set_index("path").loc[r["path"]]
        if c.line != "PV-IRES-Cre" or c.cls != "E" or r["beh"]["principal"] is None:
            continue
        d = light_design(r, "vS1")
        if d is None:
            continue
        x = auc_inputs(r, d, rng, reading)
        row = {"path": r["path"], "subject": r["subject"], "reading": reading}
        for cond in ("ctl", "light"):
            tb, ta = np.array(x[cond]["t"][0]), np.array(x[cond]["t"][1])
            nb, na = np.array(x[cond]["n"][0]), np.array(x[cond]["n"][1])
            row[f"{cond}_touch_trials"], row[f"{cond}_notouch_trials"] = len(tb), len(nb)
            row[f"{cond}_auc"] = yu2016.roc_auc((tb, nb), (ta, na), rng)
            row[f"{cond}_after"] = ta.mean() / 0.25 if len(ta) else np.nan
            row[f"{cond}_before"] = tb.mean() / 0.25 if len(tb) else np.nan
        rows_.append(row)
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows_)
    t["evoked_ctl"] = t.ctl_after - t.ctl_before
    t["auc_change"] = t.light_auc - t.ctl_auc
    return t

auc = pd.concat([auc_table(reading, np.random.default_rng(29 if reading == "a" else 31)) for reading in ("a", "b")], ignore_index=True)
for reading, g in auc.groupby("reading"):
    g = g.dropna(subset=["ctl_auc", "light_auc"])
    up, dn = g[g.auc_change > 0], g[g.auc_change < 0]
    print(f"Reading {reading}: {len(g)} cells with an AUC in both conditions (trials per cell, median: control {int(g.ctl_touch_trials.median())} touch, "
          f"{int(g.ctl_notouch_trials.median())} no-touch; light {int(g.light_touch_trials.median())} touch, {int(g.light_notouch_trials.median())} no-touch). "
          f"AUC rises in {len(up)}, falls in {len(dn)}, unchanged in {int((g.auc_change == 0).sum())}. Control touch-evoked rate (0 to 250 ms after minus "
          f"before, spikes/s): rising group mean {up.evoked_ctl.mean():.2f}, falling group mean {dn.evoked_ctl.mean():.2f} "
          f"(rank-sum p = {stats.ranksums(up.evoked_ctl, dn.evoked_ctl).pvalue:.2g}, reported only)")
    print(f"   AUC control median {g.ctl_auc.median():.3f}, light median {g.light_auc.median():.3f}")
    print(f"   Spearman correlation of AUC change with the control touch-evoked rate: rho = {stats.spearmanr(g.evoked_ctl, g.auc_change)[0]:.2f} (reported only)")
print("Cells without an AUC in a condition:", auc[auc.ctl_auc.isna() | auc.light_auc.isna()].groupby("reading").size().to_dict())

Cells without an AUC in a condition: {'a': 6, 'b': 8}

Result: not reproduced. With the fixed seeds, cells whose AUC rises with the light have a lower control touch-evoked rate than those whose AUC falls under both readings: 5.93 against 10.87 spikes/s (a) and 8.14 against 8.18 (b). The seed check below shows that reading (b) does not decide: over 20 further seeds the rising group's rate is lower in 8 and higher in 12 (8.14 to 8.53 against 7.86 to 8.18 spikes/s), while reading (a) holds in 19 of 20. The criterion needs both readings, and under (b) the sign of a 0.04 spikes/s difference is set by the resampling, so the result is not reproduced. No test separates the groups under either reading with the fixed seeds (rank-sum p = 0.37 and 1, reported only).

auc-groups¶

Neurons whose AUC rose with PV suppression gained touch-evoked spiking (3.4 to 8.7 spikes/s); neurons whose AUC fell kept their touch-evoked response (7.3 to 7.0 spikes/s) but had higher baseline rates (0.9 to 2.6 spikes/s).
