Seeds. The AUC resampling and the random no-touch windows of reading (a) depend on the generator. A reading is taken to match only when it matches under most of the 20 seeds, since an outcome that changes with the seed is not a reproduction; this rule is this attempt's, recorded as a deviation.

Result: not reproduced. With the fixed seeds the readings differ: under (a) the three tests hold (rise in the increased-AUC group, p = 4.9e-05; no change in the reduced-AUC group's touch response, p = 0.11; rise of its baseline, p = 0.0049) with group sizes (23 and 12) and rates outside tolerance, and under (b) the reduced-AUC group's touch response changes (p = 0.021). Over 20 further seeds, the three tests hold in 9 seeds under (a) and in none under (b), where the reduced-AUC group's touch response changes in every seed (p = 0.015 to 0.045). The partial result of (a) with seed 29 is the minority outcome, so neither reading matches the claim and it is not reproduced. Group sizes range from 15 to 22 (rising) and 11 to 19 (falling) over seeds.

behavior-false-alarms¶

With PV interneurons suppressed, most mice (6 of 8) are more likely to report touch with the pole out of reach (false alarms on no-lick trials).

In [38]:
rows = []
for r in l4:
    if line_of[r["subject"]] != "PV-IRES-Cre":
        continue
    d = light_design(r, "vS1")
    if d is None:
        continue
    tr = r["trials"]
    lit = np.zeros(len(tr), bool)
    lit[list(d["windows"])] = True
    nogo = tr.type.str.lower().to_numpy() == "nogo"
    cr = tr.response.to_numpy() == "CR"
    for cond, m in (("light", lit), ("ctl", d["ctl"])):
        rows.append({"subject": r["subject"], "path": r["path"], "cond": cond, "nogo": int((m & nogo).sum()), "correct": int((m & nogo & cr).sum())})
bt = pd.DataFrame(rows)

def chi(g):
    t = g.groupby("cond")[["nogo", "correct"]].sum()
    if not {"light", "ctl"} <= set(t.index):
        return pd.Series({"ctl_correct": np.nan})
    tab = np.array([[t.loc[c, "correct"], t.loc[c, "nogo"] - t.loc[c, "correct"]] for c in ("ctl", "light")])
    ok = tab.sum(axis=1).min() > 0 and tab.sum(axis=0).min() > 0
    p_y = stats.chi2_contingency(tab)[1] if ok else np.nan
    p_n = stats.chi2_contingency(tab, correction=False)[1] if ok else np.nan
    return pd.Series({"ctl_nogo": int(tab[0].sum()), "ctl_correct": tab[0, 0] / tab[0].sum(), "light_nogo": int(tab[1].sum()),
                      "light_correct": tab[1, 0] / tab[1].sum() if tab[1].sum() else np.nan, "p_yates": p_y, "p_no_correction": p_n})

pooled = bt.groupby("subject").apply(chi)
pooled["decrease_yates"] = (pooled.p_yates < 0.05) & (pooled.light_correct < pooled.ctl_correct)
pooled["decrease_plain"] = (pooled.p_no_correction < 0.05) & (pooled.light_correct < pooled.ctl_correct)
pooled["increase_yates"] = (pooled.p_yates < 0.05) & (pooled.light_correct > pooled.ctl_correct)
pooled["increase_plain"] = (pooled.p_no_correction < 0.05) & (pooled.light_correct > pooled.ctl_correct)
print("PV-IRES-Cre mice with the eNpHR light:", len(pooled), "(paper 8 tested). Reading (a), each mouse's trials pooled; correct = CR on no-lick trials:")
print(pooled.round(3).to_string())
print("Reading (a), mice with a significant decrease: (i) without the correction", int(pooled.decrease_plain.sum()), "; (ii) Yates",
      int(pooled.decrease_yates.sum()), "; significant increase: (i)", int(pooled.increase_plain.sum()), ", (ii)", int(pooled.increase_yates.sum()))
per = bt.groupby(["subject", "path"]).apply(chi).reset_index()
per["decrease"] = (per.p_yates < 0.05) & (per.light_correct < per.ctl_correct)
per["decrease_plain"] = (per.p_no_correction < 0.05) & (per.light_correct < per.ctl_correct)
ps = per.groupby("subject").agg(sessions=("path", "size"), any_decrease=("decrease", "any"), any_decrease_plain=("decrease_plain", "any"))

Expected 6 of 8 mice (reproduced at 6 under a reading, partially at 5 to 7, not reproduced below 5)

Result: reproduced. Of 9 PV-IRES-Cre mice with the light (the paper tested 8), 6 show a significant decrease of no-lick performance under reading (b)(i), per session without the continuity correction, as the criterion asks (6 of 8). The other readings give 5 ((a)(i), trials pooled, no correction), 4 ((a)(ii), pooled, Yates) and 5 ((b)(ii), per session, Yates); no mouse shows a significant increase when its trials are pooled. Reading (b) counts a mouse when any of its sessions is significant, and mice have 1 to 11 sessions, so it gives more chances to a mouse with many sessions; one session of anm244024 shows a significant rise (p = 0.042) while another shows a fall. Before the answer of 2026-10-20 the claim was blocked because the readings with and without the correction disagreed; the criterion now names both, and the reading without it matches.

Blocked claims¶

exc-inhibition-timing: With L4 excitatory neurons depolarized near 0 mV to reveal inhibition, touch evokes strong, transient inhibition that follows excitation by 0.4 +- 0.8 ms at half maximum.

exc-inhibition-whisking: In L4 excitatory neurons held near 0 mV, inhibitory inputs occur spontaneously but are more prevalent at the onset of whisker movement; after whisking onset, excitation and inhibition increase gradually, with indistinguishable time courses, over about 100 ms.

vpm-photoinhibition: Photoactivating TRN axons in VPM of VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice reduces thalamic activity to 17% of control.

rabies-vpm-input: Monosynaptic rabies tracing from L4 PV interneurons labels thalamic neurons mostly in VPM (>90%) and few in POM (<10%).

ion-cut-exc-no-touch, ion-cut-exc-whisking, ion-cut-exc-phase, ion-cut-fs-no-touch, sensory-input-drives-fs, ion-cut-fs-phase, ion-cut-behavior: after infraorbital nerve transection, L4 excitatory neurons do not depolarize after touch, their whisking depolarization and phase locking are reduced, touch does not evoke spikes in FS cells, their whisking activation is absent in most cells and their phase locking reduced, and mice perform at chance.

Result: blocked (data missing): exc-inhibition-timing and exc-inhibition-whisking. Only one whole-cell file has trials held near 0 mV, 13 trials of the PV-ChR2 cell, which Supplementary Table 2 counts as FS, and no other file pairs a whole-cell trace with a depolarizing current (data check); the 6 excitatory neurons recorded at rest and with depolarizing current are not in the dandiset.

Result: blocked (data missing): vpm-photoinhibition. No file holds a thalamic recording made with a pipette during light: the 130 single-cell files are all in barrel cortex layer 4, and the 18 VPM silicon probe files have no photostimulation series.

Result: blocked (data missing): rabies-vpm-input. The dandiset holds no histology or image data.

Result: blocked (metadata insufficient): the seven ION-cut claims. No file marks the ION-cut mice. The 4 flagged mice are consistent with them (their whole-cell excitatory cells have touch PSPs of 0.35 mV on average against 5.54 mV in the others, and their 2 FS cells 0.09 spikes per touch), but they were found by these very properties, so they cannot test the claims.

The eight claims that keep their ids have new criteria, written from the full text, so their outcomes are not the same test as before; the attempt record says for each why the outcome differs.

After the first verification round three outcomes changed. fs-touch-response is blocked as methods underspecified, since its FS readings give different outcomes (two of three values within tolerance with the waveform boundary, one without it). auc-weak-strong and auc-groups are not reproduced: over 20 further seeds, reading (b) of auc-weak-strong holds in 8, and the tests of auc-groups hold in 9 seeds under reading (a) and in none under (b). The other outcomes hold under the added readings (O11 for every whisking-epoch claim, O10 and O11 for the whisking-onset claims) and the revised tag test.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The files name no cell type and do not mark the ION-cut mice, so the cell classes are built by the claims file's rules (light tag, the waveform boundary read approximately from Supplementary Fig. 6, PV inactivation, spike width) and every group includes the cells of the ION-cut mice, which the paper left out of its control groups. The rules give 20 FS cells (17 with a principal whisker) against the paper's 26 control FS cells, and 102 excitatory cells (97 measured) against 85; 8 light-driven cells fall outside the boundary as measured here, and 26 VGAT-ChR2 cells have too few cortical light pulses to be tested and count as excitatory; among them are a whole-cell cell with 11,087 spikes 0.37 ms wide and a cell-attached cell with 16,350 spikes, which are likely FS, so the excitatory groups probably hold some FS cells. Only 3 of the paper's 4 PV cells can be found, and they are found by the inactivation the claim tests. The VPM files name one principal whisker per file. Spike detection and the spike-measure windows that the claims file leaves open are standard choices stated in the helper module; the cell-attached detection has 5% of intervals under 1.5 ms in the median E cell, and cell-attached E cells fire at several times the paper's rates; whole-cell E cells, whose detection is clean, also fire 0.70 spikes/s without whisking against the paper's 0.4. The light-driven test (a one-sided binomial test of spikes 0 to 5 ms after each pulse of the 5 and 10 Hz trains against the same 5 ms 50 ms earlier) and the waveform measures are this attempt's; the paper gives neither, and the claims file runs two thresholds and the boundary as readings. Trials of a whole-cell cell held near 0 mV are left out at rest. The derivative-based Vm latencies follow the criterion's rule, which single-sample excursions of dVm/dt and a one-sample transient at light onset cross. Where an outcome depends on a random seed (the AUC claims), a reading counts as matching only when it matches under most of 20 seeds, a rule of this attempt.

What was found about the dandiset. Every finding of the earlier attempt is still present on the same version: no cell types, no ION-cut marks, missing or partial genotypes, layer 4 for every cell, undescribed optogenetic conditions, the wrong recording mode in 24 session descriptions, a first-touch time divided by 1000, a sampling rate stated only by the timestamps, files without a principal whisker and one principal whisker per VPM file, and doubtful light wavelengths. New here: the injected current is stored in nA under a conversion to amperes that assumes uA, and 17 cell-attached files carry a constant stored current of about 1.9; the depolarized recordings of Fig. 3, the thalamic multiunits of Fig. 6b,c and the histology of Supplementary Fig. 10 are not in the dandiset; trains at the VPM site run at 50 Hz in 12 files where the Methods give 100 Hz; and the no-lick trial type is spelled two ways.
